data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 8 files and found them to be standard AUR packaging for a Node.js server application. The PKGBUILD contains typical build/package functions (yarn install, file copying, systemd unit installation) with no injected malicious code, no unexpected network requests, and no obfuscated commands. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was solely due to HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to audit PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, and LICENSE, not due to any security concerns. All successfully reviewed files (service, env, sysusers, tmpfiles, REUSE.toml) are standard declarative configuration files with no executable code.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is entirely due to tool failure, not security analysis. The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit 3 critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, LICENSE), forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. There is no actual disagreement about the security posture of the package.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, and LICENSE due to HTTP 400 API errors
learnings: API errors during file review should trigger automatic retries rather than immediately marking files as inconclusive
When the initial PKGBUILD parse audit succeeds but subsequent full file reviews fail with API errors, the tool should preserve the initial audit result rather than discarding it
The tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool failure' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' in its final verdict reporting
